ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 1 — Fannie Lou Hamer — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Establishing care at the rural community health center for high blood pressure readings, thirst and frequent urination, leg and back aching, and reduced vision in the left eye since an old injury, with consent-based, trauma-informed care and a social needs screen

text.paragraph: The patient attends this visit for establishing care at the rural community health center for high blood pressure readings, thirst and frequent urination, leg and back aching, and reduced vision in the left eye since an old injury, with consent-based, trauma-informed care and a social needs screen. [S]

Hemoglobin A1c: 8.6% (high); Glucose (random): 238 mg/dL (high); Sodium: 139 mmol/L; Potassium: 4.3 mmol/L; Creatinine: 0.96 mg/dL; eGFR (CKD-EPI 1962): 73 mL/min/1.73 m² (low); Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio: 88 mg/g (high); Total cholesterol: 228 mg/dL (high); LDL cholesterol: 146 mg/dL (high); HDL cholesterol: 44 mg/dL (low); Triglycerides: 190 mg/dL (high); ALT: 24 U/L; AST: 22 U/L; Hemoglobin: 12.6 g/dL; Platelets: 268 10*3/uL; TSH: 2.1 mIU/L; PHQ-9: 4; AHC-HRSN screen: core needs positive (0 to 5): 3. [S]

Consent-based, trauma-informed care at every visit: explain each examination, test and procedure beforehand (what it is, why, what it involves, the alternatives, including not doing it), ask her agreement and record it, offer a chaperone or companion of her choosing, let her stop at any time, never perform an unplanned procedure, and keep the plan in writing; written consent for any procedure beyond routine tests. Guideline: Trauma-Informed Care in Behavioral Health Services (Treatment Improvement Protocol 57) (2014); Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 2.1.1: Informed Consent (2026); Informed Consent and Shared Decision Making in Obstetrics and Gynecology (Committee Opinion No. 819) (2021) [S]

Nephrology consultation by telehealth from the health center, with the community health worker present, for albumin in the urine and reduced kidney function in a woman with an old kidney injury, new diabetes and high blood pressure readings. Guideline: 11. Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024) [S]

Blood pressure: a validated home monitor with a large cuff, provided by the health center, with readings twice a day for seven days to confirm the diagnosis; less salt, using foods she can get; recheck in two weeks. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, diabetes type 2, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Diabetes: metformin extended-release once daily, an A1c every three months until at goal, diabetes self-management education in a group class at the health center, and no medicine that can cause low blood sugar. Guideline: Introduction and Methodology: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, diabetes type 2, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Kidneys: repeat the urine albumin test, a kidney ultrasound with the consultation, no ibuprofen or naproxen, and kidney function and potassium checks after any blood pressure or kidney medicine is started. Guideline: 11. Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024) [S]

Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin 40 mg with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks, a baseline ECG, and TSH at diagnosis. Guideline: Introduction and Methodology: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, diabetes type 2, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Eyes and feet: retinal photographs in the clinic, so that no separate trip is needed; a comprehensive foot examination yearly; daily foot checks at home, callus care at the health center and well-fitting shoes. Guideline: 12. Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026) [S]

Social needs, with the community health worker: the AHC health-related social needs screen at intake and every few months; help applying for SNAP and the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program; the health center's food pantry and produce program; 211 for other local help; rides arranged for every visit and laboratory test; the sliding-fee scale; 90-day medicine supplies at the discount pharmacy, and phone visits when travel is not possible. Guideline: 1. Improving Care and Promoting Health in Populations: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); The Accountable Health Communities Health-Related Social Needs Screening Tool (2017); SNAP Eligibility (2026); Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (2026) [S]

Shared decisions and the team: Dr. Batiste-Hill, a nurse, the community health worker and the pharmacist review the plan with her; medicines chosen for cost, once-daily dosing and her preferences; she decides what she accepts. Guideline: Introduction and Methodology: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); Informed Consent and Shared Decision Making in Obstetrics and Gynecology (Committee Opinion No. 819) (2021) [S]

Mood and stress: PHQ-9 at intake and at four months, asked privately; counseling offered at her choice. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, diabetes type 2, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Vaccines: pneumococcal, hepatitis B and Tdap offered, explained and given only with her agreement; influenza and COVID-19 each autumn. Guideline: Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026) [S]
